name: Lola T70 Mk3B
description:
The Lola T70 Mk3B is a legendary Group 6 sports prototype racing car, representing the pinnacle of Lola Cars' development of the T70 series. Designed by Eric Broadley in 1969, the Mk3B was the ultimate evolution of a lineage that began in 1965 and dominated sports car racing on both sides of the Atlantic.

Broadley founded Lola Cars and had previously contributed to the Ford GT40 program before departing due to creative differences. The T70 embodied his original vision: a lightweight, mid-engined sports racer with innovative monocoque construction. The Mk3B featured a distinctive flat rear deck that generated 200 kg of downforce, a revolutionary concept at a time when most designers focused solely on reducing drag.

Powered by a Traco-prepared Chevrolet small-block V8 displacing 5.9 liters, the T70 Mk3B produces 550 horsepower at 7,500 RPM through a sequential gearbox. Weighing just 750 kg, the car offers an exceptional power-to-weight ratio that made it devastatingly quick through fast, sweeping corners at circuits like Spa-Francorchamps.

While the T70 series struggled in endurance events like Le Mans due to engine reliability issues with European fuel, it achieved remarkable success in shorter races such as the BOAC 500, where its superb handling and light weight proved decisive advantages against heavier competitors.
